19	 *
20	 * Key sequence (two consecutive writes to ctrl):
21	 *   1st write: (0x5A << 16) | period   — unlock
22	 *   2nd write: (0xA5 << 16) | period   — apply (WDT armed)

24	 * Feed: clear APB_WDT status bit[1:0], then reinit (same key+period).

44	#define WDT_APB_STATUS    (WDT_APB_BASE + 0x04u)   /* status (write 0 to clear bit[1:0]) */
45

48	#define WDT_AON_CTRL      WDT_AON_BASE              /* same ctrl layout */
49	
50	/* Key values (wdt_reg.h:35-36). */
51	#define WDT_KEY1          0x5Au
52	#define WDT_KEY2          0xA5u
53

56	 * the register is approximately milliseconds.  8 s covers cold-init
57	 * (worst-case ~100 ms) with 80× margin; a real hang resets in ≤ 8 s. */
58	#define WDT_PERIOD        8000u
59

61	 * (bk-official-bootloader-reverse.md §2.4, sub_2000FE4: bic.w r1,r3,#0x3F
62	 * then orr.w ip,r1,#0x26). */

64	#define WDT_SYSCTRL_VAL   0x26u

68	/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */

77	    uint32_t ctrl2;

89	    REG32(WDT_APB_CTRL) = ctrl1;
90	    REG32(WDT_APB_CTRL) = ctrl2;

92	    /* 3. Unlock + arm AON_WDT (same protocol). */
93	    REG32(WDT_AON_CTRL) = ctrl1;
94	    REG32(WDT_AON_CTRL) = ctrl2;
95	}

98	 * same period, mirroring vendor sub_2001010 (clear status + reinit).

100	static inline void boot_wdt_feed(void)
101	{
102	    uint32_t ctrl1;
103	    uint32_t ctrl2;
104	
105	    /* Clear APB_WDT status bit[1:0]. */
106	    REG32(WDT_APB_STATUS) = REG32(WDT_APB_STATUS) & ~0x3u;

108	    ctrl1 = (uint32_t)(WDT_KEY1 << 16) | (WDT_PERIOD & 0xFFFFu);

111	    /* Re-arm APB_WDT (= feed). */
112	    REG32(WDT_APB_CTRL) = ctrl1;
113	    REG32(WDT_APB_CTRL) = ctrl2;

10	 * with 64 external IRQs (NR_IRQS=80), so the table must route the
11	 * system-exception and external-IRQ slots through the full armv8-m context
12	 * saving path:
13	 *
14	 *   slots [2..3]   -> bk7258_hardfault_handler (temporary NMI/HardFault
15	 *                                               diagnostic)
16	 *   slots [4..63]  -> exception_common          (remaining exceptions,
17	 *                                               SysTick, lower external IRQs)
18	 *   slots [64]     -> BK7258_APP_MAGIC_WORD0    (boot magic, runtime-repaired)
19	 *   slots [65]     -> BK7258_APP_MAGIC_WORD1    (boot magic, runtime-repaired)
20	 *   slots [66..79] -> exception_common          (upper external IRQs)
21	 *
22	 * exception_common lives in the common armv8-m/arm_m source set that
23	 * chip/Make.defs pulls in via `include armv8-m/Make.defs`.  The actual
24	 * handlers (arm_svcall, systick_interrupt, UART ISR, ...) are attached at
25	 * runtime via irq_attach() and dispatched through g_irqvector[] by
26	 * arm_doirq(); they are not placed in the vector table directly.  We provide
27	 * this chip-specific table so the BK7236 app magic can be placed at the
28	 * fixed bootloader-validated slots [64]/[65].
29	 *
30	 * Why a chip-provided vector table (instead of the shared arm_vectors.c):
31	 *
32	 *   The on-board Tier-1 bootloader reads a 64-bit app magic "BK7236\0\0"
33	 *   from image byte offset 0x100 before it validates-and-jumps to the app
34	 *   Reset entry.  Image offset 0x100 == vector slot index 64 (0x100 / 4).
35	 *   With 64 external IRQs, the standard NuttX table is 16 + 64 = 80 entries
36	 *   (slots [0..79]), so the magic words at [64]/[65] are inside the table.
37	 *   We therefore select ARCH_HAVE_CUSTOM_VECTORS at the chip Kconfig level
38	 *   (which makes armv8-m/arm_m drop arm_vectors.c) and provide this file
39	 *   instead.  After VTOR switches to RAM, arm_ramvec_attach repairs slots
40	 *   64/65 to exception_common.
41	 *
42	 * Layout (80 entries, 0x140 bytes total; the .vectors section is pinned
43	 * at flash origin 0x02010000 by scripts/ld.script):
44	 *
45	 *   [0]      0x2809FFFC   initial MSP (top of 0x28000000..0x2809FFFF SRAM)
46	 *   [1]      __start      Reset entry (Thumb; toolchain sets bit0)
47	 *   [2..3]   bk7258_hardfault_handler (temporary diagnostic)
48	 *   [4..63]  exception_common (remaining exceptions, SysTick, lower external IRQs)
49	 *   [64]     0x32374B42   app magic word 0: "BK72" little-endian
50	 *   [65]     0x00003633   app magic word 1: "36\0\0" little-endian
51	 *   [66..79] exception_common (upper external IRQs 48..63)

53	 * Entry [64] sits at byte offset 0x100 -- exactly what the bootloader
54	 * validates.  This layout is shared verbatim with the bare-metal probe
55	 * (docs/bk7258-t5ai/probe/probe.c) that has already been boot-verified
56	 * on the T5-AI board.  Slots [0], [1], [64], [65] are UNCHANGED from N1
57	 * (the bootloader's hard requirements); only the dispatcher slots in the
58	 * middle were upgraded from spin loops to the real NuttX handlers.
59	 ****************************************************************************/
60	
61	/****************************************************************************
62	 * Included Files
63	 ****************************************************************************/
64	
65	#include <nuttx/config.h>
66	
67	#include "chip.h"
68	#include "arm_internal.h"
69	#include "ram_vectors.h"
70	#include "nvic.h"
71	
72	/****************************************************************************
73	 * Pre-processor Definitions
74	 ****************************************************************************/
75	
76	/* Top of usable SRAM (0x28000000 + 0xA0000 = 0x280A0000; keep the last
77	 * word free for safety, matching the probe).  This is what the hardware
78	 * loads into MSP from slot [0] before jumping to slot [1].
79	 */
80	
81	#define BK7258_INITIAL_MSP              0x2809fffcu
82	
83	/* App magic, little-endian.  'B''K''7''2' | '3''6''\0''\0'.
84	 * Verified against board/bootloader behaviour; see probe.c.
85	 */
86	
87	#define BK7258_APP_MAGIC_WORD0          0x32374b42u   /* "BK72" */
88	#define BK7258_APP_MAGIC_WORD1          0x00003633u   /* "36\0\0" */
89	
90	/* UART1 FIFO registers -- bare-MMIO path identical to bk7258_start.c's
91	 * bk7258_early_putc.  Duplicated here (vectors.c does not include
92	 * bk7258_start.c, which keeps bk7258_early_putc file-static).  Used only
93	 * by the diagnostic HardFault/NMI handler below.  Touches only MMIO, so it
94	 * is safe from a faulted exception context (no .data/.bss dependency).
95	 */
96	
97	#define BK7258_FAULT_UART1_FIFO_STAT    (*(volatile unsigned int *)0x45830018u)
98	#define BK7258_FAULT_UART1_FIFO_PORT    (*(volatile unsigned int *)0x4583001Cu)
99	#define BK7258_FAULT_UART1_FIFO_READY   (1u << 20)
100	
101	/****************************************************************************
102	 * Permanent A1 compile-time invariants
103	 *
104	 * These assertions verify the A1 IRQ/vector definitions at compile time.
105	 * They use #ifdef / _Static_assert(0) branches so the gate fires if a
106	 * required macro is ever removed.
107	 *
108	 * Placement: after chip.h and nvic.h have exposed NR_IRQS,
109	 * ARMV8M_PERIPHERAL_INTERRUPTS, and NVIC priority macros.
110	 ****************************************************************************/
111	
112	/* --- Core IRQ count gates --- */
113	
114	#ifdef BK7258_EXTERNAL_IRQS
115	  _Static_assert(BK7258_EXTERNAL_IRQS == 64,
116	                 "A1 gate: BK7258_EXTERNAL_IRQS must be 64");
117	#else
118	  _Static_assert(0,
119	                 "A1 gate: BK7258_EXTERNAL_IRQS not defined; expected 64");
120	#endif
121	
122	_Static_assert(NR_IRQS == 80,
123	               "A1 gate: NR_IRQS must be 80 (16 + 64 external)");
124	
125	_Static_assert(ARMV8M_PERIPHERAL_INTERRUPTS == 64,
126	               "A1 gate: ARMV8M_PERIPHERAL_INTERRUPTS must be 64 (external IRQ count)");
127	
128	/* --- Vector table sizing --- */
129	
130	/* ARM_VECTAB_SIZE is defined by arch/arm/src/arm_m/ram_vectors.h as
131	 * (ARMV8M_PERIPHERAL_INTERRUPTS + NVIC_IRQ_FIRST), i.e. 64 + 16 = 80.
132	 * Assert its expected A1 value; conditional branch handles the case
133	 * where the common header has not yet been included.
134	 */
135	
136	#ifdef ARM_VECTAB_SIZE
137	  _Static_assert(ARM_VECTAB_SIZE == 80,
138	                 "A1 gate: ARM_VECTAB_SIZE must be 80");
139	#else
140	  _Static_assert(0,
141	                 "A1 gate: ARM_VECTAB_SIZE not defined; expected 80");
142	#endif
143	
144	#ifdef VECTAB_ALIGN
145	  _Static_assert(VECTAB_ALIGN == 512,
146	                 "A1 gate: VECTAB_ALIGN must be 512");
147	#else
148	  _Static_assert(0,
149	                 "A1 gate: VECTAB_ALIGN not defined; expected 512");
150	#endif
151	
152	/* --- IRQ anchor gates (future A1 production names) --- */
153	
154	#ifdef BK7258_IRQ_ETHERNET
155	  _Static_assert(BK7258_IRQ_ETHERNET == 64,
156	                 "A1 gate: ETHERNET must be NuttX IRQ 64");
157	#else
158	  _Static_assert(0,
159	                 "A1 gate: BK7258_IRQ_ETHERNET not defined; expected 64");
160	#endif
161	
162	#ifdef BK7258_IRQ_SCALE0
163	  _Static_assert(BK7258_IRQ_SCALE0 == 65,
164	                 "A1 gate: SCALE0 must be NuttX IRQ 65");
165	#else
166	  _Static_assert(0,
167	                 "A1 gate: BK7258_IRQ_SCALE0 not defined; expected 65");
168	#endif
169	
170	#ifdef BK7258_IRQ_MAILBOX
171	  _Static_assert(BK7258_IRQ_MAILBOX == 79,
172	                 "A1 gate: MAILBOX must be NuttX IRQ 79");
173	#else
174	  _Static_assert(0,
175	                 "A1 gate: BK7258_IRQ_MAILBOX not defined; expected 79");
176	#endif
177	
178	/* --- Magic slot / offset structural gates --- */
179	
180	#define BK7258_MAGIC_SLOT0      64      /* vector slot for magic word 0 */
181	#define BK7258_MAGIC_SLOT1      65      /* vector slot for magic word 1 */
182	
183	_Static_assert(BK7258_MAGIC_SLOT0 * 4 == BK7258_MAGIC_BOOT0_OFFSET,
184	               "A1 gate: magic slot 64 must be at flash offset 0x100");
185	_Static_assert(BK7258_MAGIC_SLOT1 * 4 == BK7258_MAGIC_BOOT1_OFFSET,
186	               "A1 gate: magic slot 65 must be at flash offset 0x104");
187	
188	/* Standard armv8-m exception dispatch entrypoints (assembly / C stubs that
189	 * save context, decode the IRQ number from IPSR, call arm_doirq(), and on
190	 * return perform a context switch if needed).  Provided by the common
191	 * armv8-m source set.
192	 */
193	
194	extern void exception_common(void);
195	
196	/* Chip entry point (defined in bk7258_start.c).  Slot [1] keeps pointing
197	 * at __start, exactly as N1 / the probe; NuttX expects the symbol to be
198	 * called __start (see nuttx/arch/arm/src/arm_m/arm_vectors.c).
199	 */
200	
201	extern void __start(void);
202	
203	/* Diagnostic HardFault/NMI handler (defined below).  Replaces the silent
204	 * exception_common spin on slots [2] (NMI) and [3] (HardFault) only, so a
205	 * trap during early boot is visible on UART1.  Pure diagnostic: it prints
206	 * "HF" and parks; it does NOT decode the fault frame and does NOT recover.
207	 */
208	
209	void bk7258_hardfault_handler(void);
210	
211	/****************************************************************************
212	 * Private Functions
213	 ****************************************************************************/
214	
215	/* Bare polled UART1 output -- freestanding, MMIO-only, identical to the
216	 * bk7258_early_putc() in bk7258_start.c.  Duplicated here because vectors.c
217	 * does not include bk7258_start.c (whose bk7258_early_putc is file-static)
218	 * and because the fault handler must not depend on any .data/.bss state.
219	 */
220	
221	static void bk7258_fault_putc(unsigned char c)
222	{
223	  while ((BK7258_FAULT_UART1_FIFO_STAT & BK7258_FAULT_UART1_FIFO_READY) == 0)
224	    {
225	    }
226	
227	  BK7258_FAULT_UART1_FIFO_PORT = (unsigned int)(c & 0xffu);
228	}
229	
230	/****************************************************************************
231	 * Public Functions
232	 ****************************************************************************/
233	
234	/* Diagnostic HardFault/NMI handler.  Pushes "HF" out over UART1 using the
235	 * same bare-MMIO write as the N2 marker, then parks forever.  NO fault
236	 * frame decode, NO recovery, NO lockup-safe spin -- pure visibility for
237	 * board-side bring-up.  Wired into vector slots [2] (NMI) and [3]
238	 * (HardFault) so either a faulting instruction or an escalated exception
239	 * becomes observable; all other system-exception slots ([4..14]) keep
240	 * routing through exception_common.
241	 */
242	
243	void bk7258_hardfault_handler(void)
244	{
245	  bk7258_fault_putc('H');
246	  bk7258_fault_putc('F');
247	  for (; ; )
248	    {
249	    }
250	}
251	
252	/* DIAGNOSTIC SysTick probe (temporary).  Wired into slot [15] INSTEAD of
253	 * exception_direct so we can tell whether the SysTick exception ENTRY itself
254	 * works on this board.  Prints 's', disables the SysTick interrupt (clears
255	 * SYST_CSR.TICKINT so it does not re-fire), and returns normally (a plain
256	 * exception return).  If 's' shows on UART1, the CPU entered the handler =>
257	 * exception entry/return are fine and the real hang is inside NuttX's
258	 * dispatch (exception_direct -> arm_doirq -> systick_interrupt) or the
259	 * PendSV context switch.  If 's' does NOT appear, exception ENTRY is broken
260	 * (vector fetch / VTOR / stack / fault on entry).  Pure diagnostic; revert.
261	 */
262	void bk7258_systick_probe(void)
263	{
264	  bk7258_fault_putc('s');
265	  *(volatile unsigned int *)0xE000E010u &= ~(1u << 1);  /* SYST_CSR.TICKINT off */
266	}
267	
268	/****************************************************************************
269	 * Public Data
270	 ****************************************************************************/
271	
272	/* The NuttX arm_m layer looks up symbol "_vectors" and section ".vectors".
273	 * `used` prevents the compiler from dropping the table at LTO; `aligned(4)`
274	 * keeps each 4-byte slot naturally aligned.
275	 *
276	 * The table is sized explicitly at 80 entries (0x140 bytes) so the two
277	 * app-magic words at [64]/[65] are inside the table and the upper external
278	 * IRQ slots [66..79] are included.  After VTOR switches to RAM,
279	 * arm_ramvec_attach repairs slots 64/65 to exception_common.
280	 *
281	 * GCC range designated initializers fill the dispatcher slots the same way
282	 * arm_vectors.c does; the magic slots [64]/[65] are then pinned explicitly
283	 * (they are runtime-repaired after RAM vector init).
284	 */
285	
286	__attribute__((section(".vectors"), used, aligned(4)))
287	const void *const _vectors[80] =
288	{
289	  /* [0]    initial MSP (loaded by hardware before __start). */
290	  [0]  = (void *)BK7258_INITIAL_MSP,
291	
292	  /* [1]    Reset entry (Thumb; toolchain sets bit0). */
293	  [1]  = (void *)__start,
294	
295	  /* [2..3] NMI + HardFault -> diagnostic bk7258_hardfault_handler.
296	   *   Replaces the silent exception_common spin on these two slots so a
297	   *   trap during early boot is visible (prints "HF" on UART1 then parks).
298	   *   NMI ([2]) is wired the same way so an escalated fault is observable.
299	   *   Pure diagnostic -- no frame decode, no recovery.
300	   */
301	  [2]  = &bk7258_hardfault_handler,
302	  [3]  = &bk7258_hardfault_handler,
303	
304	  /* [4..14] remaining system exceptions -> exception_common
305	   *   4=MemManage 5=BusFault 6=UsageFault 7=SecureFault 8..10=Reserved
306	   *   11=SVCall 12=DebugMonitor 13=Reserved 14=PendSV
307	   */
308	  [4 ... 14]  = &exception_common,
309	
310	  /* Route SysTick and lower external IRQs through the full context-saving
311	   * exception path.  SysTick is board-verified on this path; routing the
312	   * external slots the same way is the first UART RX IRQ recovery step. */
313	
314	  [15 ... 63] = &exception_common,
315	
316	  /* [64] app magic word 0: "BK72" little-endian.  Byte offset 0x100. */
317	  [64] = (void *)BK7258_APP_MAGIC_WORD0,
318	
319	  /* [65] app magic word 1: "36\0\0" little-endian. Byte offset 0x104. */
320	  [65] = (void *)BK7258_APP_MAGIC_WORD1,
321	
322	  /* [66..79] upper external IRQs -> exception_common
323	   *   These slots correspond to external IRQs 48..63.  Slots 64/65 are
324	   *   overwritten by the boot magic above and must be runtime-repaired
325	   *   via arm_ramvec_attach after VTOR switches to RAM.
326	   */
327	  [66 ... 79] = &exception_common
328	};

6	 * Beken BK7258 (T5-AI, Cortex-M33) SysTick system-timer init for NuttX.
7	 *
8	 * Modelled on nuttx/arch/arm/src/mps/mps_timer.c.  up_timer_initialize()
9	 * loads the SysTick reload value for the configured tick rate and registers
10	 * the common armv8-m SysTick lower half (arm_systick.c) as the system clock
11	 * source.
12	 *
13	 * Clock assumptions (see docs/bk7258-t5ai + armino sdkconfig.h):
14	 *   - The Tier-1 bootloader does NOT enable the DPLL; the app core runs at
15	 *     the BootROM default = the 26 MHz XTAL.  Hence CONFIG_CPU_FREQ_HZ =
16	 *     26000000.
17	 *   - SysTick CLKSOURCE = processor clock (no /8 divisor), so the SysTick
18	 *     clock equals CONFIG_CPU_FREQ_HZ.
19	 *
20	 *   Reload = cpu_hz / CLK_TCK - 1, where cpu_hz is decoded at runtime from
21	 *            the live clock registers by bk7258_clockdiag_current_cpu_hz():
22	 *
23	 *              baseline (M1=0, dplle=0)         -> 26000000 Hz
24	 *              loader --reboot 1 (M1=0x423)     -> 80000000 Hz
25	 *              unknown                           -> 26000000 Hz (fallback)
26	 *
27	 *            No DPLL/mux/voltage/UART-divisor write is performed; only the
28	 *            SysTick reload bookkeeping is recomputed.
29	 *
30	 *   BOARD_CPU_FREQ_HZ in board.h remains the build-time baseline / fallback
31	 *   and matches the runtime baseline-case return; it is no longer used
32	 *   directly in the reload path.
33	 ****************************************************************************/

55	 * Pre-processor Definitions
56	 ****************************************************************************/
57	
58	/* SysTick reload for one OS tick is computed at runtime in
59	 * up_timer_initialize() from bk7258_clockdiag_current_cpu_hz() and CLK_TCK
60	 * (= 1000000 / CONFIG_USEC_PER_TICK).  BOARD_CPU_FREQ_HZ (board.h) remains
61	 * the documented build-time baseline and equals the baseline-case runtime
62	 * return, but is no longer used directly in the reload path.
63	 */
64	
65	/****************************************************************************
66	 * Public Functions
67	 ****************************************************************************/
68	
69	/****************************************************************************
70	 * Name: up_timer_initialize
71	 *
72	 * Description:
73	 *   Called during start-up (up_initialize) to initialise the timer
74	 *   hardware that drives the NuttX system clock.  Registers the common
75	 *   Cortex-M SysTick lower half, clocked at the runtime-detected cpu_hz.
76	 *
77	 ****************************************************************************/
78	
79	void up_timer_initialize(void)
80	{
81	  uint32_t cpu_hz;
82	  uint32_t reload;
83	
84	  /* Decode the runtime core-clock frequency from the live M1/ANA_REG5
85	   * state (read-only) and derive the SysTick reload for one OS tick.  No
86	   * DPLL, mux, voltage or UART-divisor write is performed -- only the
87	   * SysTick reload bookkeeping is recomputed.
88	   *
89	   *   Baseline (M1=0, dplle=0):      cpu_hz = 26000000
90	   *   Loader --reboot 1 (M1=0x423):  cpu_hz = 80000000
91	   *
92	   * systick_initialize() will then arm CLKSOURCE | TICKINT (core clock,
93	   * interrupt on wrap) and attach the SysTick ISR; setting the reload first
94	   * guarantees the first tick has the correct period (some QEMU/model cores
95	   * ignore CTRL writes when RELOAD is zero, so follow the mps_timer.c
96	   * ordering).
97	   */
98	
99	  cpu_hz = bk7258_clockdiag_current_cpu_hz();
100	  reload = (cpu_hz / CLK_TCK) - 1;
101	
102	  putreg32(reload, NVIC_SYSTICK_RELOAD);
103	
104	  /* coreclk=true  -> SysTick clocked at the processor clock (cpu_hz).
105	   * minor=-1      -> do not register a /dev/timerN node; this timer is the
106	   *                  dedicated system clock only.
107	   */
108	
109	  up_timer_set_lowerhalf(systick_initialize(true, cpu_hz, -1));
110	}
111	
112	/****************************************************************************
113	 * Name: bk7258_systick_recalc
114	 *
115	 * Description:
116	 *   Recompute and atomically rewrite the SysTick one-tick reload for the
117	 *   live core clock, after a runtime DVFS frequency switch.  SysTick is
118	 *   clocked at the CPU0 processor clock (CLKSOURCE = processor clock, no
119	 *   /8 divisor), so every CPU frequency change must update RELOAD here or
120	 *   the OS tick period drifts (sleep N becomes N * (old_hz / new_hz)).
121	 *
122	 *   Reads M1/ANA_REG5 via bk7258_clockdiag_current_cpu_hz() (read-only) and
123	 *   writes only RELOAD + CVR.  Clearing CVR after touching RELOAD is the
124	 *   ARMv8-M architecturally mandated sequence to apply a new reload on the
125	 *   next wrap (CVR is write-to-clear).
126	 *
127	 *   This keeps the NuttX common arm_systick.c upstream untouched (the
128	 *   systick_lowerhalf_s.freq field is NOT updated here -- it is only used
129	 *   for usec/count conversions in optional timer APIs, not for the tick
130	 *   cadence, which is governed by RELOAD).  If a future caller needs
131	 *   accurate usec-scale timeouts after a switch, that is a separate task.
132	 *
133	 *   Caller (bk7258_dvfs_set_freq) holds interrupts disabled across the
134	 *   whole mux+reload sequence, so no extra irqsave is taken here.
135	 *
136	 ****************************************************************************/
137	
138	#ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_DVFS
139	void bk7258_systick_recalc(void)
140	{
141	  uint32_t cpu_hz;
142	  uint32_t reload;
143	
144	  cpu_hz = bk7258_clockdiag_current_cpu_hz();
145	  reload = (cpu_hz / CLK_TCK) - 1;
146	
147	  /* Use the BK7258_CDIAG_SYSTICK_* address macros (always present in
148	   * bk7258_clockdiag.h) rather than risking a backend-specific
149	   * NVIC_SYSTICK_CURRENT definition.  RVR is RELOAD, CVR is the
150	   * write-to-clear current-counter register. */
151	  putreg32(reload, BK7258_CDIAG_SYSTICK_RVR);
152	
153	  /* Write any value to CVR to clear it; the SysTick then counts down from
154	   * RELOAD so the first tick is one full tick long at the new period. */
155	  putreg32(0, BK7258_CDIAG_SYSTICK_CVR);
156	}
157	#endif /* CONFIG_BK7258_DVFS */

52	#ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_FLASH_LITTLEFS
53	/* LittleFS bring-up: register /dev/mtdblock0 (ftl), mount at /data with the
54	 * "autoformat" option (formats only on first boot), then run a probe-file
55	 * persistence check.
56	 *
57	 * The probe file is created on the first boot after format and read back on
58	 * every later boot, so a reboot observing the expected bytes proves write
59	 * persistence.
60	 */
61	
62	#define BK7258_FS_MOUNTPOINT  "/data"
63	#define BK7258_FS_BLOCKDEV    "/dev/mtdblock0"
64	#define BK7258_FS_PROBE       "/data/probe.txt"
65	#define BK7258_FS_PROBE_LEN   12
66	static const char g_fs_probe[BK7258_FS_PROBE_LEN] = "BK7258LFS-OK";
67	
68	static void bk7258_fs_probe(struct mtd_dev_s *mtd)
69	{
70	  char buf[BK7258_FS_PROBE_LEN];
71	  int fd;
72	  ssize_t n;
73	
74	  if (ftl_initialize(0, mtd) < 0)
75	    {
76	      return;
77	    }
78	
79	  mkdir(BK7258_FS_MOUNTPOINT, 0777);
80	
81	  if (mount(BK7258_FS_BLOCKDEV, BK7258_FS_MOUNTPOINT, "littlefs", 0,
82	            "autoformat") < 0)
83	    {
84	      return;
85	    }
86	
87	  /* If the probe file exists, read it back and compare (persistence). */
88	
89	  fd = open(BK7258_FS_PROBE, O_RDONLY);
90	  if (fd < 0)
91	    {
92	      /* First boot: create the probe file. */
93	
94	      fd = open(BK7258_FS_PROBE, O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_TRUNC, 0666);
95	      if (fd < 0)
96	        {
97	          return;
98	        }
99	
100	      if (write(fd, g_fs_probe, BK7258_FS_PROBE_LEN) != BK7258_FS_PROBE_LEN)
101	        {
102	          close(fd);
103	          return;
104	        }
105	
106	      close(fd);
107	      sync();
108	      return;
109	    }
110	
111	  n = read(fd, buf, BK7258_FS_PROBE_LEN);
112	  close(fd);
113	
114	  /* Persistence verification: the file was created on a previous boot, so a
115	   * successful read-back of the expected marker proves writes survive reset.
116	   * Stay silent when persistence is confirmed; log a runtime error otherwise.
117	   */
118	
119	  if (n != (ssize_t)BK7258_FS_PROBE_LEN ||
120	      memcmp(buf, g_fs_probe, BK7258_FS_PROBE_LEN) != 0)
121	    {
122	      _err("bk7258: LittleFS probe persistence check failed (n=%d)\n",
123	           (int)n);
124	    }
125	}

137	 *   CONFIG_NSH_ARCHINIT from the NSH init task.  Mounts procfs at
138	 *   CONFIG_NSH_PROC_MOUNTPOINT (default /proc) and returns OK.
139	 *

152	#endif

154	  /* Register the BK7258 DVFS /proc/dvfs entry *before* mounting procfs: the
155	   * fs_procfs NOTE requires the procfs entry table to be stable at mount
156	   * time (procfs_register reallocs the table; doing it after the mount would
157	   * race with concurrent procfs access). */
158	
159	#if defined(CONFIG_FS_PROCFS) && defined(CONFIG_BK7258_DVFS_PROCFS)
160	  (void)bk7258_dvfs_procfs_register();
161	#endif

163	  /* Mount procfs at the NSH proc mountpoint so ps, ls /proc, and cat of
164	   * /proc entries work.  CONFIG_NSH_ARCHINIT activates this hook;
165	   * CONFIG_FS_PROCFS provides the filesystem.
166	   */
167	
168	  (void)mount(NULL, CONFIG_NSH_PROC_MOUNTPOINT, "procfs", 0, NULL);
169	
170	#ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_FLASH_MTD
171	  /* Create the MTD instance for the 1 MiB data partition.  When LittleFS is
172	   * also enabled, register /dev/mtdblock0 + mount /data and run the probe
173	   * persistence check on the same instance.
174	   */
175	
176	  FAR struct mtd_dev_s *mtd = bk7258_flash_mtd_initialize();
177	  if (mtd != NULL)
178	    {
179	#ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_FLASH_LITTLEFS
180	      bk7258_fs_probe(mtd);
181	#endif
182	    }
183	#endif
184	
185	  return 0;
186	}

7	 *
8	 * Mirrors the Armino SDK WDT BSP path:
9	 *   bk_wdt_driver_init  -> wdt_hal_init (select WDT unit, close unused)
10	 *                        -> bk_timer_start(TIMER_ID2, 1s, feed_handle)
11	 *   bk_wdt_start(ms)    -> wdt_init_common (power up clock)
12	 *                        -> wdt_hal_init_wdt -> wdt_ll_set_period
13	 *                            (global_ctrl.soft_reset=1,
14	 *                             key1(0x5A)+period, key2(0xA5)+period)
15	 *   bk_wdt_feed()       -> wdt_hal_init_wdt(hal, period)  (= reinit)
16	 *   bk_wdt_stop()       -> close_wdt (key1+period=0, key2+period=0)
17	 *
18	 * NuttX watchdog upper-half (CONFIG_WATCHDOG_AUTOMONITOR) handles periodic
19	 * feeding via work queue once /dev/watchdog0 is opened and started.
20	 * The lower-half only implements the hardware operations.
21	 *
22	 * The Tier-1 bootloader arms the APB WDT during cold-init to recover from
23	 * DPLL / SPI hangs.  This driver takes over after boot: it reinitializes
24	 * the WDT with the configured period (default 8 s) and registers as
25	 * /dev/watchdog0.  The bootloader's WDT remains armed during the handoff

1	/****************************************************************************
2	 * contest2026_135_yongwangzhiqian/board/bk7258_t5ai/chip/bk7258_wdt.c
3	 *
4	 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
5	 *
6	 * BK7258 (T5-AI) hardware watchdog NuttX lower-half driver.
7	 *
8	 * Full WDT BSP, mirroring the Armino SDK WDT driver path
9	 * (cp/middleware/driver/wdt/wdt_driver.c + wdt_hal.c + wdt_ll.h):
10	 *
11	 *   SDK path                          NuttX equivalent
12	 *   ─────────────────────────────     ──────────────────────────
13	 *   bk_wdt_driver_init()              bk7258_wdt_initialize()
14	 *     wdt_hal_init()                    (select APB WDT, no AON switching)
15	 *     bk_timer_start(TIMER_ID2,...)     (NuttX automonitor handles feed)
16	 *     aon_pmu_drv_wdt_rst_dev_enable() (already done by bootloader)
17	 *   bk_wdt_start(timeout_ms)          bk7258_wdt_start()
18	 *     wdt_init_common()                 (WDT clock already on)
19	 *     wdt_hal_init_wdt → set_period     key1+period, key2+period
20	 *   bk_wdt_feed()                     bk7258_wdt_keepalive()
21	 *     wdt_hal_init_wdt(hal, period)     (= reinit with same period)
22	 *   bk_wdt_stop()                     bk7258_wdt_stop()
23	 *     close_wdt()                       key1+period=0, key2+period=0
24	 *
25	 * NuttX watchdog upper-half (CONFIG_WATCHDOG_AUTOMONITOR) handles periodic
26	 * feeding via work queue once /dev/watchdog0 is opened and started.
27	 * We do not need a separate TIMER_ID2 or IRQ-based feed loop.
28	 *
29	 * The bootloader arms the APB WDT with period=8000 (~8 s) during cold-init.
30	 * This driver reinitializes the WDT with the same or user-configured period
31	 * and keeps it alive.  The bootloader does NOT close WDT before jumping
32	 * (matching vendor behavior: sub_200176C has no WDT close code).
33	 ****************************************************************************/
34	
35	/****************************************************************************
36	 * Included Files
37	 ****************************************************************************/
38	
39	#include <nuttx/config.h>
40	
41	#ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_WDT
42	
43	#include <stdint.h>
44	#include <errno.h>
45	#include <debug.h>
46	
47	#include <nuttx/timers/watchdog.h>
48	
49	#include "arm_internal.h"
50	#include "bk7258_wdt.h"
51	
52	/****************************************************************************
53	 * Pre-processor Definitions
54	 ****************************************************************************/
55	
56	/* APB WDT register addresses (wdt_reg.h, wdt_struct.h). */
57	
58	#define BK7258_WDT_BASE           0x44800000u
59	#define BK7258_WDT_GLOBAL_CTRL    (BK7258_WDT_BASE + 0x08u)
60	#define BK7258_WDT_CTRL           (BK7258_WDT_BASE + 0x10u)  /* period+key */
61	#define BK7258_WDT_STATUS         (BK7258_WDT_BASE + 0x04u)  /* status, clear bit[1:0] to feed */
62	
63	/* SYS block (for SYS_CTRL WDT clock/reset config, matching bootloader). */
64	
65	#define BK7258_SYS_CTRL_REG       0x44000008u
66	
67	/* WDT key values (wdt_reg.h:35-36). */
68	
69	#define BK7258_WDT_KEY1           0x5Au
70	#define BK7258_WDT_KEY2           0xA5u
71	
72	/* WDT field masks (wdt_reg.h). */
73	
74	#define BK7258_WDT_PERIOD_MASK    0xFFFFu
75	#define BK7258_WDT_KEY_SHIFT      16
76	
77	/* Default timeout: 8000 ms (matches SDK CONFIG_INT_WDT_PERIOD_MS and
78	 * bootloader's WDT_PERIOD).  The WDT clock is ~1 kHz, so period in the
79	 * register is approximately milliseconds. */
80	
81	#define BK7258_WDT_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS  8000u
82	
83	/* SYS_CTRL bits[5:0] = 0x26: vendor WDT clock/reset config. */
84	
85	#define BK7258_WDT_SYSCTRL_MASK   0x3Fu
86	#define BK7258_WDT_SYSCTRL_VAL    0x26u
87	
88	/****************************************************************************
89	 * Private Types
90	 ****************************************************************************/
91	
92	struct bk7258_wdt_lowerhalf_s
93	{
94	  struct watchdog_lowerhalf_s wdt_lh;  /* Must be first */
95	  uint32_t timeout;                    /* Current timeout in ms */
96	  bool     started;                    /* WDT is armed */
97	};
98	
99	/****************************************************************************
100	 * Private Function Prototypes
101	 ****************************************************************************/
102	
103	static int bk7258_wdt_start(struct watchdog_lowerhalf_s *lower);
104	static int bk7258_wdt_stop(struct watchdog_lowerhalf_s *lower);
105	static int bk7258_wdt_keepalive(struct watchdog_lowerhalf_s *lower);
106	static int bk7258_wdt_getstatus(struct watchdog_lowerhalf_s *lower,
107	                                struct watchdog_status_s *status);
108	static int bk7258_wdt_settimeout(struct watchdog_lowerhalf_s *lower,
109	                                 uint32_t timeout);
110	
111	/****************************************************************************
112	 * Private Data
113	 ****************************************************************************/
114	
115	static const struct watchdog_ops_s g_bk7258_wdt_ops =
116	{
117	  .start      = bk7258_wdt_start,
118	  .stop       = bk7258_wdt_stop,
119	  .keepalive  = bk7258_wdt_keepalive,
120	  .getstatus  = bk7258_wdt_getstatus,
121	  .settimeout = bk7258_wdt_settimeout,
122	};
123	
124	static struct bk7258_wdt_lowerhalf_s g_bk7258_wdt;
125	
126	/****************************************************************************
127	 * Private Helpers
128	 ****************************************************************************/
129	
130	/* Write the two-step key sequence to WDT_CTRL (mirrors wdt_ll_set_period).
131	 * The first write with key1 unlocks; the second with key2 applies the period. */
132	
133	static inline void bk7258_wdt_write_period(uint32_t period)
134	{
135	  putreg32((BK7258_WDT_KEY1 << BK7258_WDT_KEY_SHIFT) |
136	           (period & BK7258_WDT_PERIOD_MASK),
137	           BK7258_WDT_CTRL);
138	
139	  putreg32((BK7258_WDT_KEY2 << BK7258_WDT_KEY_SHIFT) |
140	           (period & BK7258_WDT_PERIOD_MASK),
141	           BK7258_WDT_CTRL);
142	}
143	
144	/****************************************************************************
145	 * Private: lower-half operations
146	 ****************************************************************************/
147	
148	static int bk7258_wdt_start(struct watchdog_lowerhalf_s *lower)
149	{
150	  struct bk7258_wdt_lowerhalf_s *priv =
151	    (struct bk7258_wdt_lowerhalf_s *)lower;
152	
153	  /* Ensure SYS_CTRL WDT config (bootloader already did this, but be
154	   * defensive: if NuttX is entered via a path that skipped the bootloader,
155	   * the WDT clock might not be configured). */
156	
157	  uint32_t v = getreg32(BK7258_SYS_CTRL_REG);
158	  v = (v & ~BK7258_WDT_SYSCTRL_MASK) | BK7258_WDT_SYSCTRL_VAL;
159	  putreg32(v, BK7258_SYS_CTRL_REG);
160	
161	  /* Soft-reset the WDT state machine (mirrors wdt_ll_set_period). */
162	
163	  putreg32(1u, BK7258_WDT_GLOBAL_CTRL);
164	
165	  /* Arm the WDT with the configured period. */
166	
167	  bk7258_wdt_write_period(priv->timeout);
168	
169	  priv->started = true;
170	  wdinfo("started, timeout=%" PRIu32 " ms\n", priv->timeout);
171	  return OK;
172	}
173	
174	static int bk7258_wdt_stop(struct watchdog_lowerhalf_s *lower)
175	{
176	  struct bk7258_wdt_lowerhalf_s *priv =
177	    (struct bk7258_wdt_lowerhalf_s *)lower;
178	
179	  /* Disarm: key sequence with period=0 (mirrors wdt_hal_close for BK7236,
180	   * wdt_hal.c:116-125). */
181	
182	  putreg32(1u, BK7258_WDT_GLOBAL_CTRL);
183	  putreg32(BK7258_WDT_KEY1 << BK7258_WDT_KEY_SHIFT, BK7258_WDT_CTRL);
184	  putreg32(BK7258_WDT_KEY2 << BK7258_WDT_KEY_SHIFT, BK7258_WDT_CTRL);
185	
186	  priv->started = false;
187	  wdinfo("stopped\n");
188	  return OK;
189	}
190	
191	/* keepalive = reinit with same period (SDK bk_wdt_feed = wdt_hal_init_wdt
192	 * with same period, wdt_driver.c:172-180). */
193	
194	static int bk7258_wdt_keepalive(struct watchdog_lowerhalf_s *lower)
195	{
196	  struct bk7258_wdt_lowerhalf_s *priv =
197	    (struct bk7258_wdt_lowerhalf_s *)lower;
198	
199	  /* Feed = clear status + reinit with same period.
200	   * Matches the bootloader's boot_wdt_feed() which works:
201	   *   clear APB_WDT status bit[1:0], then key1+period, key2+period.
202	   * Do NOT soft_reset here — soft_reset may clear the WDT clock gate
203	   * (the SDK's wdt_init_common() re-powers the clock after soft_reset,
204	   * but we don't have that call in keepalive). */
205	
206	  putreg32(getreg32(BK7258_WDT_STATUS) & ~0x3u, BK7258_WDT_STATUS);
207	  bk7258_wdt_write_period(priv->timeout);
208	  return OK;
209	}
210	
211	static int bk7258_wdt_getstatus(struct watchdog_lowerhalf_s *lower,
212	                                struct watchdog_status_s *status)
213	{
214	  struct bk7258_wdt_lowerhalf_s *priv =
215	    (struct bk7258_wdt_lowerhalf_s *)lower;
216	
217	  status->flags = WDFLAGS_RESET;
218	  if (priv->started)
219	    {
220	      status->flags |= WDFLAGS_ACTIVE;
221	    }
222	
223	  status->timeout = priv->timeout;
224	
225	  /* timeleft: we cannot read the current counter from the BK7258 APB WDT
226	   * (no readable counter register).  Return timeout as an upper bound. */
227	
228	  status->timeleft = priv->timeout;
229	  return OK;
230	}
231	
232	static int bk7258_wdt_settimeout(struct watchdog_lowerhalf_s *lower,
233	                                 uint32_t timeout)
234	{
235	  struct bk7258_wdt_lowerhalf_s *priv =
236	    (struct bk7258_wdt_lowerhalf_s *)lower;
237	
238	  if (timeout > BK7258_WDT_PERIOD_MASK)
239	    {
240	      timeout = BK7258_WDT_PERIOD_MASK;
241	    }
242	
243	  priv->timeout = timeout;
244	
245	  /* If already running, re-arm with new period. */
246	
247	  if (priv->started)
248	    {
249	      bk7258_wdt_write_period(priv->timeout);
250	    }
251	
252	  wdinfo("timeout set to %" PRIu32 " ms\n", priv->timeout);
253	  return OK;
254	}
255	
256	/****************************************************************************
257	 * Public Functions
258	 ****************************************************************************/
259	
260	/****************************************************************************
261	 * Name: bk7258_wdt_initialize
262	 *
263	 * Description:
264	 *   Initialize the BK7258 APB WDT and register as /dev/watchdog0.
265	 *   Mirrors the SDK bk_wdt_driver_init + bk_wdt_start path:
266	 *     - Select APB WDT (the bootloader already configured SYS_CTRL and
267	 *       AON/ABP WDT key sequences; we re-assert the config defensively).
268	 *     - Set default period (8 s, matching bootloader WDT_PERIOD).
269	 *     - Register the NuttX watchdog lower-half.
270	 *
271	 *   After registration, opening /dev/watchdog0 and calling start enables
272	 *   CONFIG_WATCHDOG_AUTOMONITOR (if configured), which feeds the WDT
273	 *   automatically via work queue.
274	 *
275	 *   Call this from board_app_initialize() (bk7258_bringup.c), after procfs
276	 *   mount and before DVFS or other long-running init.
277	 *
278	 ****************************************************************************/
279	
280	int bk7258_wdt_initialize(void)
281	{
282	  struct bk7258_wdt_lowerhalf_s *priv = &g_bk7258_wdt;
283	
284	  priv->wdt_lh.ops = &g_bk7258_wdt_ops;
285	  priv->timeout    = BK7258_WDT_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS;
286	  priv->started    = false;
287	
288	  /* The bootloader already armed the WDT (period=8000, SYS_CTRL=0x26).
289	   * We don't re-arm here — start() does that when the upper-half opens
290	   * the device.  This matches the SDK pattern where bk_wdt_driver_init
291	   * does NOT call bk_wdt_start; the caller decides when to arm. */
292	
293	  watchdog_register("/dev/watchdog0",
294	                    (struct watchdog_lowerhalf_s *)priv);
295	
296	  wdinfo("BK7258 WDT registered as /dev/watchdog0, default timeout=%" PRIu32
297	         " ms\n", priv->timeout);
298	  return OK;
299	}
300	
301	#endif /* CONFIG_BK7258_WDT */

# BK7258 N6：约 4295 秒后 `HF` + 重启根因

日期：2026-07-23

状态：**根因已由源码与当前 ELF 反汇编确认；尚未修改配置、构建或板测。**

## 现象

系统正常启动并进入 NSH，运行约 4200 秒以上后输出：

```text
HFu_bootloader enter
```

随后重新启动。多次运行均在相近时间复现。

## 日志解释

源码中的 bootloader 字符串实际是：

```text
u_bootloader enter
```

位于 `board/bk7258_t5ai/bootloader/boot_main.c:187`。

`HF` 来自 `board/bk7258_t5ai/chip/bk7258_vectors.c:243-249` 的临时故障处理器。该处理器同时占用向量槽 2（NMI）和槽 3（HardFault），因此当前日志不能区分 NMI 与 HardFault。结合后述喂狗链，最可能是 APB WDT 超时产生的 NMI；`F` 与下一次启动的 `u_bootloader enter` 相连，形成 `Fu_bootloader enter`。

## 已确认根因

当前配置为：

```text
CONFIG_TIMER_ARCH=y
CONFIG_USEC_PER_TICK=10000
CONFIG_SYSTEM_TIME64 未启用
```

因此 `clock_t` 是 32 位。NuttX 通用 arch timer 在 `nuttx/drivers/timers/arch_timer.c:97-110` 中计算微秒时间：

```c
return TICK2USEC(timebase) + (status.timeout - status.timeleft);
```

而 `nuttx/include/nuttx/clock.h:168` 定义：

```c
#define TICK2USEC(tick) ((tick) * USEC_PER_TICK)
```

`timebase` 为 32 位 `clock_t`，所以乘法在 32 位中完成后才扩展为函数返回的 `uint64_t`。溢出点为：

```text
2^32 us = 4294967296 us = 4294.967296 s
```

当前 `nuttx` ELF 的 `current_usec()` 反汇编也直接证明了这一点：地址 `0x0201537a` 使用单个 32 位 `mla` 完成 `timebase * 10000 + sub_tick_usec`，返回值高 32 位被置零。

## 为什么最终会重启

1. `nuttx/drivers/timers/arch_timer.c:265-275` 的 `up_timer_gettick()` 使用 `current_usec() / USEC_PER_TICK`。
2. `CONFIG_TIMER_ARCH=y` 时，`nuttx/sched/clock/clock_systime_ticks.c:89-95` 的 `clock_systime_ticks()` 调用 `up_timer_gettick()`。
3. 每个系统 tick 中，`nuttx/sched/sched/sched_processtimer.c:179-200` 把该值传给 `wd_timer()`，用于处理 NuttX watchdog/软件定时器绝对到期时间。
4. 到 4294.967296 秒时，系统对外报告的 tick 从约 `429496` 突然折返到 `0`，而活动 watchdog 节点的绝对到期值仍在约 `429xxx`。
5. 软件 watchdog 队列因此把这些节点误判为“还需等待约 4295 秒”，其中包括硬件 WDT automonitor 的下一次喂狗回调。
6. BK7258 配置为 APB WDT 8 秒超时、每 2 秒自动喂一次：
   - `CONFIG_WATCHDOG_AUTOMONITOR_TIMEOUT=8`
   - `CONFIG_WATCHDOG_AUTOMONITOR_PING_INTERVAL=2`
7. automonitor 停止执行后，APB WDT 在约 8 秒内触发 NMI/复位，形成 `HF` 后重启。

因此预计实际复位时间约为 4295 秒再加最后一次喂狗到超时的 6～8 秒，和板端“超过 4200 秒后稳定复现”完全一致。

## 最小 overlay 修复

不修改官方 `nuttx/` 树，在团队板级 defconfig 中启用：

```text
CONFIG_SYSTEM_TIME64=y
```

这样 `clock_t` 变为 64 位，`TICK2USEC(timebase)` 的乘法也会在 64 位中执行，消除 4295 秒折返。

建议同时在 BK7258 Kconfig/构建门禁中约束：使用 `CONFIG_TIMER_ARCH` 时必须启用 `CONFIG_SYSTEM_TIME64`，防止以后 defconfig 回退。

## 上游正确修复

NuttX 通用实现应在乘法前显式扩展：

```c
return (uint64_t)timebase * USEC_PER_TICK +
       (uint64_t)(status.timeout - status.timeleft);
```

但本项目规则是不直接修改官方 `nuttx/` checkout；如需上游修复，应走独立社区 PR。

## 相关但不是本次直接根因的问题

`bk7258_os_adapt.c` 中还存在：

```c
nxsig_usleep(milliseconds * 1000);
```

其 32 位毫秒转微秒也会在大参数时溢出，应后续单独修复。但本次无需任何“大延时调用”：系统基础 tick 转微秒本身就会在 4294.967296 秒必然折返，因此它才是当前稳定重启的直接根因。

## 待验证

1. 在团队 overlay defconfig 增加 `CONFIG_SYSTEM_TIME64=y`。
2. 重新构建并烧录。
3. 连续运行越过 4400 秒；在 4280、4310、4400 秒附近读取 `/proc/uptime`，确认单调递增。
4. 确认不再出现 `HFu_bootloader enter`，且 WDT、LittleFS、DVFS、UART/NSH 无回归。
5. 后续把 NMI 与 HardFault 日志拆分，避免 `HF` 二义性。

## 根因已确认

这不是普通的“大延时参数溢出”，而是 **NuttX 系统 tick 在 4294.967296 秒被错误折返为 0**，随后喂狗定时器失效，最终 WDT 触发复位。

### 直接证据

当前配置：

```text
CONFIG_TIMER_ARCH=y
CONFIG_USEC_PER_TICK=10000
CONFIG_SYSTEM_TIME64 未启用
```

因此 `clock_t` 为 32 位：`nuttx/include/sys/types.h:254-259`。

通用 arch timer 计算微秒时间：

```c
return TICK2USEC(timebase) + (status.timeout - status.timeleft);
```

位置：`nuttx/drivers/timers/arch_timer.c:97-110`

而宏定义是：

```c
#define TICK2USEC(tick) ((tick) * USEC_PER_TICK)
```

位置：`nuttx/include/nuttx/clock.h:168`

乘法发生在 32 位中，所以必然在：

```text
2^32 us = 4294967296 us = 4294.967296 s
```

发生回卷。

当前 ELF 反汇编也确认了：`current_usec()` 在 `0x0201537a` 使用单条 32 位 `mla` 计算 `timebase * 10000 + sub_tick`，返回值高 32 位直接为零。这已经不是推测。

## 完整故障链

1. `up_timer_gettick()` 使用回卷后的 `current_usec()`：
   `nuttx/drivers/timers/arch_timer.c:265-275`
2. `CONFIG_TIMER_ARCH=y` 时，系统 tick 从这里读取：
   `nuttx/sched/clock/clock_systime_ticks.c:89-95`
3. 每个 SysTick 都把这个时间传给软件 watchdog 队列：
   `nuttx/sched/sched/sched_processtimer.c:197-200`
4. 到 4294.967 秒，tick 从约 `429496` 突然跳到 `0`。
5. 已经排队的 WDT automonitor 回调到期值仍是约 `429xxx`，被误认为还要等待约 4295 秒。
6. APB WDT 自动喂狗停止；当前配置是每 2 秒喂、8 秒超时。
7. 最后一次喂狗后的 6～8 秒，WDT 触发 NMI/复位。

所以预计重启点约为：

```text
4294.967 + 6～8 秒 ≈ 4301～4303 秒
```

与你看到的“每次超过 4200 秒后稳定重启”完全一致。

## 为什么输出是 `HFu_bootloader enter`

真实 bootloader 字符串只有：

```text
u_bootloader enter
```

位于 `contest2026_135_yongwangzhiqian/board/bk7258_t5ai/bootloader/boot_main.c:187`。

当前向量槽 2（NMI）和槽 3（HardFault）都指向同一个诊断处理器，它打印 `HF`：

`contest2026_135_yongwangzhiqian/board/bk7258_t5ai/chip/bk7258_vectors.c:234-249`

因此：

```text
HF + u_bootloader enter
```

拼成了：

```text
HFu_bootloader enter
```

这里的 `HF` **不能证明是 HardFault**；结合上述喂狗链，最可能是 APB WDT 的 NMI。

## 最小修复

不修改官方 `nuttx/` 树，只需在团队 overlay 的 defconfig 中启用：

```text
CONFIG_SYSTEM_TIME64=y
```

这样 `clock_t` 变成 64 位，`TICK2USEC(timebase)` 的乘法也会以 64 位完成。

长期上游修复应该是：

```c
return (uint64_t)timebase * USEC_PER_TICK +
       (uint64_t)(status.timeout - status.timeleft);
```

但按照项目规则，不应直接改当前官方 NuttX checkout。

另外，`bk7258_os_adapt.c` 中的 `milliseconds * 1000` 也有潜在溢出，但它不是这次稳定重启的直接根因。

## 当前处理状态

- 未修改源码或 defconfig
- 未构建、未烧录
- 因 IRQ 会话当前正在修改同一个 defconfig，我没有写入，避免并发冲突

  `contest2026_135_yongwangzhiqian/docs/bk7258-t5ai/nuttx-port/n6-bug-4295s-timer-wrap.md`
